transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have a civil subpoena on hand requesting customer analytics records, related communications, and a source-code appendix, and we're on a 10-calendar-day clock to respond in writing. Before I approve our response strategy and any commitments we make to the requesting party, I need each of you to report any issues that must be addressed. Let's start with investigations — what are you seeing?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, before we go further on response strategy, I need to flag a conflict issue. I completed a conflict-database check this morning and found that our usual outside litigation firm, Harrison & Cole, currently represents the subpoenaing party in an unrelated matter. That creates a conflict that prevents Harrison & Cole from advising us on this subpoena. I've already cleared Merritt Legal as a replacement firm, but I hadn't circulated the check result yet, so I'm surfacing it now. We should factor this into our response planning, since we'll need to bring Merritt Legal up to speed within our 10-day window.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag an issue on the e-discovery side. My document review of the responsive collection found exactly 47 attorney-client privileged emails and exactly 312 customer records containing Social Security numbers. These counts are not yet reflected in the draft response spreadsheet because quality control of the export finished after the spreadsheet was circulated to the case team. We need to address both the privilege hold on those 47 emails and the PII concern with the 312 customer records containing SSNs before the response is approved.
